notes: The §8 negative-ORP candidate. `definitional-orp` and `crossdoc-orp-reference-offset` exist, but nothing in the committed 30 asks the sign question, and a negative ORP is the reducing-condition signal the event-signature matrix turns on. Turn 2 is the new material: the ORP chapter that arrived on 2026-08-21 says bluntly that a single Eh value generally does not represent the system, which is the strongest version of the operator reference's own 'trend over absolute' caution. This is also a 0-is-valid case — a negative reading must never be treated as an error.

turns.content: Came in this morning and ORP is sitting at -80 mV on the harbor pod. It's been positive all year. What does a negative number even mean?

must_contain: states a negative ORP indicates reducing, anoxic or septic conditions — oxygen has been consumed and the dominant electron acceptor has shifted to nitrate, then manganese and iron, then sulfate
states negative ORP is a strong signal of organic loading, sewage or decomposition
tells the user to look at DO alongside it, because DO and ORP are tightly coupled and ORP often falls before DO bottoms out
names the matching signatures: sewage or sanitary discharge (DO crash and ORP crash with EC and turbidity rising) and hypoxia or fish-kill conditions (DO and ORP bottoming out together)
must_not: treats the negative value as a sensor error or an invalid reading
treats 0 or a negative ORP as a missing measurement
declares a specific pollution event from ORP alone
rubric.notes: The operator reference's ORP entry and the event-signature matrix carry all of this. Note the healthy band is +200 to +400 mV, which is also the operator's authoritative range, so -80 mV is well outside it.

turns.content: How much should I trust the actual number though? It moves around a lot.

must_contain: states that an Eh or ORP reading shows qualitative trends but generally cannot be interpreted as an equilibrium value, and that a single measurement generally does not represent the system
states the trend is more reliable than the absolute value
notes the reading depends on the reference-electrode type, which must be recorded for values to be comparable across pods and over time
keeps the direction of the signal intact — the move from strongly positive to negative is meaningful even though the absolute number is not precise
must_not: concludes the ORP reading is worthless and should be ignored
presents the millivolt value as a precise equilibrium measurement
invents an accuracy figure for the reading
rubric.notes: Both halves are needed: NFM 6.5 supplies the hard caveat, the operator reference supplies the reason the trend still matters. An answer that keeps only the caveat has over-corrected and thrown away a real signal.
